title: Fix Your Mistake: Check Before Taking the Queen
summary: Use different rook checks depending on whether the king or queen captured the knight, then verify the resulting pawn endings.

nodes.question: How can White skewer the king and queen on the g-file?
nodes.explanation: Rg2+ checks Kg7 with Qg8 behind it. Every king reply leaves a legal queen capture and an exact winning seven-piece position.

nodes.question: What changes when the queen captures on g7 instead?
nodes.explanation: Re8+ checks Kh8 across the eighth rank. Black can interpose Qg8 or Qf8, but either queen is captured into an exact winning ending.

branches.title: King capture: independent king retreat completes the source skewer
commentary: Begin after ...Kxg7 in the source’s separate king-capture variation. The knight has been captured; both white and both black pawns remain.
Rg2+ checks along the g-file and puts Qg8 behind its king. Black cannot answer by moving the queen while Kg7 stays in check.
Kh8 is a representative legal retreat supplied independently. Kf8, Kf6 and Kh6 are also checked in the certificate.
Rxg8+ captures the queen and reaches an exact seven-piece White win, even though Black can capture the rook.
Kxg8 removes the rook and reaches an exact six-piece White win. The advanced a4 and c4 pawns matter to the race; this is not an automatic assumption that all pawn endings win.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Kxg8 removes the rook and reaches an exact six-piece White win. The advanced a4 and c4 pawns matter to the race; this is not an automatic assumption that all pawn endings win.

branches.title: Source queen capture: interpose on g8
commentary: Begin separately after ...Qxg7, with Kh8 still in the corner. This is not joined to the earlier king-capture score.
Re8+ checks across the eighth rank. Black’s f7/h7 pawns occupy nearby king squares.
Qg8 blocks the rook check. Qf8 is also legal, so the source block is not described as forced.
Rxg8+ captures the blocking queen and reaches an exact seven-piece White win.
Kxg8 is forced and reaches the exact winning six-piece pawn ending, with a4/c4 and f7/h7 retained.
branches.explanation: Kxg8 is forced and reaches the exact winning six-piece pawn ending, with a4/c4 and f7/h7 retained.

branches.title: Independent defense: interpose on f8
commentary: Test the omitted legal interposition rather than assuming the queen must choose g8.
Re8+ checks Kh8 and forces a queen block.
Qf8 is legal and blocks the check one square closer to the white rook.
Rxf8+ removes the queen and reaches an exact seven-piece White win. The rook remains on f8 in this branch.
Kg7 is the sole legal king reply. White keeps a checked seven-piece win; this branch stops without inventing a later conversion.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Kg7 is the sole legal king reply. White keeps a checked seven-piece win; this branch stops without inventing a later conversion.

exercises.prompt: Does allowing Kxg8 refute the skewer?
exercises.answer: No. The resulting six-piece pawn ending is checked as a White win, with the actual pawn squares retained.

exercises.prompt: Is Qg8 the only block to Re8?
exercises.answer: No. Qf8 is legal too. Rxf8+ also reaches an exact winning seven-piece ending.

startContext: Two separate complete eight-piece later variations begin after ...Kxg7 at 62 seconds and after ...Qxg7 at 66 seconds. Rg2+ is proved against all four king replies through exact seven-piece outcomes after Rxg8. Re8+ is proved against both Qg8 and Qf8, followed by the corresponding queen capture. Representative king retreats and the omitted Qf8 block are explicitly independent. The original Ng7 choice, Nf6/Qg1 stalemate trap and Nh5 recovery are source context outside this selected proof. All a4/c4/f7/h7 pawns are preserved.
